sovereign_country.strategic_role: 极速离岸证券与外汇交易商持牌（VFSC）、轻资产免税出海

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Remote Desktop Access and Unattended Machine Telemetry Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English common law, French civil law, and customary law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: No comprehensive bilateral investment treaty network as of record date; Vanuatu relies on domestic investment law and PACER Plus trade disciplines.
Tax Information Exchange Agreements (TIEAs) in force with multiple OECD jurisdictions; does not constitute a DTAA for income tax purposes.
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations (PACER Plus) signatory.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Proliferation Financing Act, No. 24 of 2018 (as amended); International Companies Act [CAP 222] (as amended); Financial Intelligence Unit Act; and the VFSC AML/CFT supervisory directions and guidance notes.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (confidential non-public UBO register maintained by the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission; accessible only to the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit and competent law enforcement authorities in accordance with AML/CFT statutes. Nominee arrangements are subject to mandatory beneficial ownership disclosure to the VFSC.)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of the document holder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuing state is a Contracting Party; otherwise consular legalization through the nearest Vanuatu diplomatic or consular post

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed financial institution in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuing state is a Contracting Party; otherwise consular legalization through the nearest Vanuatu diplomatic or consular post

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-holding bank in the client's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Professional services firm in the client's country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory identification and risk-rating of all directors, shareholders, authorized signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners as Politically Exposed Persons. Required screening against the United Nations Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN List, UK/EU consolidated sanctions lists, and the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit's national enforcement and watch-list notices. Enhanced due diligence is required for PEPs and for any individual or entity identified on the FATF public statements or connected to high-risk jurisdictions. Screening results must be documented and retained for at least 5 years after the business relationship ceases.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) Company Registry E-Portal — https://www.vfsc.vu/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be submitted in Roman/Latin script. English, French, or Bislama names are accepted; names in non-Latin scripts require a certified English transliteration. An International Company must end with 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Société Anonyme', 'S.A.', or another prescribed suffix under the International Companies Act.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the VFSC issues a formal refusal notice stating the statutory grounds. The applicant may file a written appeal with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 calendar days of the refusal, setting out the proposed name, legal basis for clearance, and any VFSC feedback incorporated. If the written appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Supreme Court of Vanuatu within 30 days. The original reservation cannot be extended beyond 30 days; a fresh name reservation application and fee are required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted for statutory registered-office purposes. An International Company must maintain a physical registered office in Vanuatu through a licensed registered agent. A purely virtual address or P.O. Box is insufficient. The business may operate entirely from abroad for this low-risk remote desktop software export activity, but the registered office must remain a physical Vanuatu address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated below 5%) for an unlicensed offshore software and remote-support company with no local employees or physical operations. Inspection risk would rise if the company name includes licensed-activity tokens, if sensitive payment flows appear, or if sanctions screening triggers adverse media.

VFSC International Company incorporation filing fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act [Cap. 222] of Vanuatu, Part 2, ss. 2–12 (incorporation, registered office, agent, directors); regulated under the Company and Trust (Licensing) Act [Cap. 92] for the licensed registered agent.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) – International Companies Registry, Port Vila
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Constitution) submitted via VFSC Form IC-01 (Application for Incorporation)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow deposit requirement. Default authorized capital USD 1,000 divided into 1,000 shares of USD 1.00 each; shares may be fully paid on allotment at par.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED that the incorporation of the Company under the International Companies Act [Cap. 222] of the Republic of Vanuatu, through the Memorandum and Articles of Association filed with the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission, be ratified and adopted. RESOLVED FURTHER that the subscriber's subscription to 100 fully paid ordinary shares of USD 1.00 each at par be accepted and allotted accordingly. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office of the Company shall be the licensed registered agent's premises in Port Vila, Vanuatu, and that [Director Name] be and is hereby appointed as the sole Director and [Secretary Name] as Company Secretary, with full authority to execute statutory records, open banking accounts and operate payment platforms, including Stripe and Paddle.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission, International Companies Registry – online eRegistry filing through a VFSC-licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two proposed corporate names carrying the suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd' via the VFSC eRegistry. The name must not be identical to a reserved name, must avoid prohibited terms (bank, insurance, trust, government patronage), and must align with the declared remote software publishing scope. A cleared name is reserved for 30 days pending incorporation.
required_dossiers: Certified passport copy of each proposed subscriber
Brief business description confirming ISIC 6201 software scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file alternative names within 5 business days or submit a written requisition to the Registrar for reconsideration; an adverse name determination is appealable to the Minister of Finance under the International Companies Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of VFSC-Licensed Registered Agent and KYC Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC-licensed registered agent (licensed under the Company and Trust (Licensing) Act [Cap. 92])
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the registered-agent engagement letter and deliver the complete KYC package for the agent's statutory customer-due-diligence assessment. The agent prepares the draft Constitution and confirms that the Company will not trade with Vanuatu residents and will not conduct banking, insurance, or trust business.
required_dossiers: Corporate services questionnaire with source-of-funds declaration
Passport copies and address proof of beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any CDD deficiency is cured by supplementary declarations or evidence; if the agent declines engagement on unresolved AML concerns, a substitute VFSC-licensed agent may be appointed without loss of priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Constitution (Memorandum and Articles of Association)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC-licensed registered agent; Vanuatu notary public or apostille authority for overseas signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The subscriber executes the Constitution subscribing for one or more shares and signs the statutory declarations confirming the absence of local Vanuatu business activity. The registered agent signs its consent to act, and the first director and company secretary execute their consents, with witness signatures notarized where required.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association (Constitution)
Subscriber declaration ancillary to Form IC-01
Consent to act as company secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Constitution is incomplete or improperly witnessed, a conformed copy is re-executed within 3 business days; notarization or apostille is accepted as conclusive evidence of signature for overseas subscribers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Application for Incorporation with VFSC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission – International Companies Registry (filing executed by the licensed registered agent via eRegistry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent files VFSC Form IC-01 together with the executed Constitution, statutory declarations, registered-office particulars, and proof of payment of the state incorporation fee. The application designates the Port Vila registered office and the first director and secretary.
required_dossiers: Consent of registered agent and statutory particulars
Proof of registered-office address in Port Vila
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VFSC issues a requisition, the registered agent responds within 14 days with corrected documents; a contested refusal may be appealed to the Minister of Finance within 30 days of the decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Entity Identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission – Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, VFSC issues the Certificate of Incorporation stating the company number and date of incorporation. The Company acquires separate legal personality, limited liability, and statutory exemption from Vanuatu income tax and exchange control. The registered agent obtains a Certificate of Good Standing for subsequent banking and payment-rail onboarding.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Good Standing (requested on issuance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A provisional confirmation may be obtained pending certificate printing; clerical errors in the certificate (name, date, number) are rectified by a formal certificate correction request to the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of First Board Resolutions, Share Allotment, and Corporate Kit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company board of directors, recorded by the VFSC-licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene and adopt the first board resolution allotting 100 fully paid ordinary shares to the subscriber, approving the registered office and registered agent, appointing the director(s) and secretary, and authorizing opening of bank accounts and payment-platform accounts (Stripe, Paddle). Open statutory registers and issue share certificates.
required_dossiers: Register of members and register of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director becomes disqualified or resigns after allotment, an ordinary resolution substitutes a replacement director and the VFSC register of directors is updated within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Compliance Setup and Banking/Payment-Rails Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC annual-compliance interface; corporate banks and payment processors (Stripe, Paddle) KYC units
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Calendar the annual return and VFSC annual fee to fall within the anniversary window. Obtain a current Certificate of Good Standing for KYC. Complete corporate bank account opening and activate Stripe/Paddle merchant accounts using the Certificate of Incorporation, register of directors, and the board resolution authorizing payment rails. No Vanuatu Business Licence is required as the Company transacts exclusively with non-residents.
required_dossiers: Register of directors and share register
Board resolution authorizing bank and payment-rail accounts
Passports and address proof of signatories and beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a financial institution requires enhanced diligence, provide a notarized certificate of incumbency and updated good-standing extract; if an account is declined, re-file KYC with alternative banking partners through the registered agent's correspondent desk.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for pure ISIC 6201 remote software publishing; if a physical presence is established, the relevant authority is the Business Licence Office, Department of Finance, Port Vila.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Exempt – International Companies are outside the scope of the Vanuatu Business Licence regime (Business Licence Act [Cap. 14]) provided they do not trade with Vanuatu residents; no sectoral software or telecommunications operating permit is triggered by remote screen-sharing/IoT telemetry services delivered abroad.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation (DEPC), Ministry of Climate Change
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category 4 (office/software services) under the Environmental Protection and Conservation Act [Cap. 283]; no EIA registration, preliminary assessment, or environmental report is required in the absence of physical manufacturing, land-clearing, or emissions-generating activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge, wastewater, VOC, or waste-handling thresholds are triggered by the remote software activity; if a physical data-centre or branch office is later opened, DEPC registration and compliance with the Vanuatu National Water Quality Standards and Waste Management Regulations (e-waste segregation and disposal certificates) would apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire safety, structural load, or workplace clearance is required for a virtual non-physical operation; if a local office is opened, the following would apply: (i) fire safety certificate from the Vanuatu Fire Services prior to occupancy, (ii) structural load inspection certificate for the premises, and (iii) workplace electrical and occupational health clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act No. 24 of 2017.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Vanuatu Revenue and Customs (VRC), Ministry of Finance and Economic Management, e-services portal vrc.gov.vu; company registry administered by Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), vfsc.vu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Section 3 of the International Companies Act [Cap 222] exempts the International Company from all Vanuatu taxes, so no VRC tax file, TIN or VAT ID is required; the VFSC incorporation certificate, registry number and annual exemption fee receipt form the de facto tax identity. SOP: (1) incorporate through a licensed registered agent under the International Companies Act; (2) obtain VFSC certificate and pay the annual government fee; (3) maintain certificate of incumbency and good standing for foreign banking and payment provider onboarding; (4) if VFSC authorization for domestic activity were ever granted (not applicable to this remote screen-share SaaS export scope), VRC would then issue a VAT registration number under the Value Added Tax Act [Cap 248].
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Vanuatu is a unitary national jurisdiction without check-the-box, sub-federal, participation exemption or hybrid mismatch elections. Re-domiciling as a domestic company under the Companies Act [Cap 191] requires dissolution and fresh incorporation, not a tax election; a tax-exempt International Company files no income tax, transfer pricing or country-by-country returns.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) - Value Added Tax Act No. 18 of 1998 [Cap 248], administered by VRC; no provincial or municipal sales and use tax overlay.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VUV 5,000,000 of taxable supplies in any preceding 12-month period for ordinary businesses; not triggered by the tax-exempt International Company, which is statutorily outside the VAT net and ring-fenced from domestic supplies to Vanuatu residents.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. No real-time fiscal clearance, transaction-level API reporting, digital stamping or mandatory B2B e-invoicing requirement. VAT returns are lodged electronically through the VRC E-Services portal; commercial invoices in PDF or ERP format are lawful. Customs declarations are processed through the ASYCUDA World national single window.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: VAT Act s.6 zero-rates exported goods and services supplied to non-residents where the benefit is enjoyed wholly outside Vanuatu, provided the supplier is VAT-registered and holds evidence of the offshore supply. For VU_IC the analysis is superseded by statutory exemption: offshore ISIC 6201 software licensing, remote screen-share access and IoT telemetry service income is outside the VAT system entirely, with no registration right or refund claim, provided customers are non-resident and no Vanuatu taxable establishment or domestic end-user exists.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: ASYCUDA World consolidated Customs Export Declaration covering any physical IoT devices or hardware shipped
Commercial invoice plus software licence and remote services agreement identifying the non-resident counterparty and ISIC 6201 scope
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for physical consignments; for pure digital delivery, server logs, IP-based usage telemetry and delivery evidence substitute
Inward remittance proof: SWIFT MT103, payment provider settlement report or receivable ledger linked to the foreign client
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating and export claims attract VAT Act penalties: civil default assessment up to 200% of the VAT evaded, monthly late-payment accruals on unpaid VAT, fines up to VUV 500,000 and imprisonment up to 2 years for knowingly false declarations. VRC audit tests match customs or offshore-service documentation to banking and payment provider FX inflows and verify the absence of Vanuatu-resident end-users and on-island delivery. An International Company breaching its legal ring-fence faces VFSC fines, revocation of exempt status and compulsory strike-off, with retrospective clawback of any VAT improperly zero-rated or refunded. Vanuatu imposes no exchange controls or statutory FX repatriation deadline; 180 days is retained as a prudential AML and payment provider benchmark.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of Vanuatu (RBV) established under the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu Act, acting as the sole monetary authority and exchange-control administrator under the Exchange Control Act, in coordination with the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) as the regulator and registrar of International Companies. The practical gatekeepers are the four licensed Authorized Dealers: ANZ Bank (Vanuatu) Limited, Bank of South Pacific (Vanuatu) Limited, BRED Bank Vanuatu Limited, and National Bank of Vanuatu Limited, each empowered to operate SWIFT, administer Foreign Currency Accounts, and execute VUV conversion trades.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Vanuatu Vatu (VUV) operates under a managed arrangement pegged to a trade-weighted basket of major trading-partner currencies; current-account convertibility is unrestricted for residents executing through an Authorized Dealer with underlying commercial documentation, while capital-account movements require standard AD due diligence rather than discretionary central-bank approval. An International Company (IC) carries a statutory exchange-control exemption under the International Companies Act, enabling unrestricted inbound equity, unrestricted repatriation of profits and liquidation proceeds, and retention of 100% of export receipts in USD, EUR, GBP, AUD, or VUV accounts without conversion obligation. The material constraint is offshore deliverability: the VUV has no active offshore market, spot liquidity is shallow outside the Authorized Dealer network, and USD-VUV conversion costs widen outside ANZ/BSP; therefore the treasury baseline should be USD-denominated concentration with VUV usage limited to local statutory spend.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Vanuatu imposes no fixed percentage surrender ratio for export receipts. The Exchange Control regime requires resident exporters to repatriate proceeds to a local Authorized Dealer account within six months of export and to either convert into VUV or credit a Foreign Currency Account in accordance with the RBV exchange-control operating manual. Non-resident International Companies are exempt from mandatory repatriation, surrender, and conversion; they may retain all software and SaaS service receipts in eligible foreign currency accounts indefinitely. Where VUV is required for on-island obligations, conversion is executed at the Authorized Dealer prevailing buying rate with the supporting IC corporate file and an underlying expense instruction.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Non-Resident Operational USD Multi-Currency Account; Capital Escrow-capable Foreign Currency Account
Operational VUV/USD Account; SWIFT GPI Trade and Settlement Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-Low. Vanuatu has no domestic EMI or payment-institution licensing regime analogous to PSD2; offshore fintech EMIs (United Kingdom, European Union, Singapore, or Hong Kong) generally classify Vanuatu-domiciled International Companies as jurisdictionally high-risk due to Vanuatu's current FATF increased-monitoring status and the absence of a local operating subsidiary. The legally compliant architecture is a principal tier-1 Vanuatu bank account paired with upstream merchant acquirers Stripe and Paddle, whose payout batches settle via SWIFT to the local bank; an EMI may be used only as a supplementary expense-card or disbursement wallet where the EMIs upstream correspondent is ANZ, BSP, or a reputable broker. Any EMI relationship must be disclosed in the bank's KYC refresh; undisclosed aggregator wallets constitute a material compliance breach and invite account restriction.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Vanuatu statutes do not prescribe universal physical attendance by every director, but the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act (No. 4 of 2006), VFSC directives, and tier-1 bank policies require full beneficiary-owner verification and a live recorded interview, either in person at the Port Vila branch or through a secure video-conference session. Remote opening is permitted for low-risk digital-services International Companies on condition that the VFSC-licensed registered agent attends the branch to lodge certified formation documents and the original board resolution authorizing account opening is delivered by courier; however, a fully unattended, interview-free onboarding is not available. For structures with layered non-resident shareholders, a physical or verified remote interview with the controller and a source-of-wealth memorandum will be enforced before SWIFT GPI payout privileges are activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity created by nominee shareholders, bearer shares, or layered intermediate holding entities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified register of members; a UBO schedule identifying every natural person with a 10% or greater interest; VFSC Certificate of Good Standing; registered-agent attestation; professional bank and legal references; plus a written source-of-wealth statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FATF grey-list jurisdiction risk and downstream correspondent-bank scrutiny on payments from Vanuatu
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate-substance file comprising board minutes, VFSC annual filings, statutory tax-exemption certificate, product documentation for remote-desktop and telemetry software, executed SaaS master agreements, Stripe/Paddle merchant settlement statements, and a typed KYC questionnaire reconciling expected transaction flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face onboarding, electronically signed resolutions, and the absence of wet-ink documents
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized passports and proof-of-address for all directors and UBOs; apostilled powers of attorney where available; dual-execution wet-ink board resolutions; a recorded video-conference interview transcript; and a compliance undertaking to provide audited financial statements annually or on regulatory demand.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Zero paid-in capital and perceived absence of economic activity or substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Account-purpose memorandum; 12-month cash-flow and transaction-velocity forecast; VFSC-registered-office services agreement; technology infrastructure contracts; merchant revenue projections from Paddle and Stripe; and confirmation that the International Company maintains a real commercial treasury profile despite its statutory tax-exempt status.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder capital should be injected via SWIFT MT103 (using MT202 for two-legged cover where size warrants) from the parent to the IC's USD concentration account at ANZ or BSP Vanuatu, with the payment narrative quoting BPM6 purpose code 5212 (Direct Investment – Equity Capital) and the receiving compliance pack containing a board resolution, share subscription or capital contribution agreement, and the VFSC return of allotment evidencing issuance. The IC's exchange-control exemption removes central-bank pre-approval, but source-of-funds evidence and clean parent-company banking references must pre-date the transfer to satisfy the receiving bank. Stripe and Paddle merchant settlements constitute cross-border service-export receipts and should be verified through payout statements mapped to EBOPS category 1800 (Telecommunications, Computer and Information Services) and directed into the same USD concentration ledger, never converted into VUV at the gateway stage, to preserve base-currency matching and avoid double conversion costs.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound operating disbursements (hosting, software procurement, independent contractors, director fees, marketing, and legal or agent fees) should be executed as SWIFT MT103 messages on the GPI network through ANZ or BSP, with each payment tagged to a sub-ledger purpose code that matches the underlying agreement, and a board-approved payment ladder enforcing dual-approval controls. For physical procurement or hardware-associated trade, the acceptable clearing instrument is an irrevocable Letter of Credit issued under ICC UCP 600, or documentary collections where the transaction is low-value; however, the remote-screen-share SaaS model will predominantly rely on Paddle and Stripe upstream aggregation and subsequent SWIFT sweeps into the Vanuatu account. Treasury policy should require D+1 settlement visibility, a single USD concentration account, and a segregated disbursement sub-account for VFSC agent and statutory fees to preserve an audit-ready trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forward Contracts (VUV/USD, VUV/EUR, VUV/AUD) available onshore through ANZ, BSP, and BRED as Authorized Dealers
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDF) on VUV executed offshore for hedging where physical VUV deliverable cannot be settled outside Vanuatu
Cross-Currency Swaps (USD/VUV principal and interest exchange) matched to long-dated shareholder loans or capital-repatriation schedules
FX Swaps (spot versus forward rollover) for temporary USD-to-VUV liquidity positioning without instantaneous spot conversion risk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) – Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the first anniversary of incorporation and annually thereafter on the same anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of Vt 5,000 (approx. USD 45) and late renewal penalty per month; continued non-compliance for 3 months after notice may result in administrative strike-off from the International Companies Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent Annual Confirmation and Agent Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) – Licensed Registered Agent in Vanuatu
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with the annual return on each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to renew the registered agent arrangement may cause VFSC to reject the annual return and initiate notification of default, leading to late fees and potential administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Vanuatu Business Licence Renewal (if commercial activities trigger licensing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Department of Customs and Inland Revenue / Municipal Authority or VFSC (as applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 January for the current calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal penalties of 10% per month on unpaid licence fee; continued non-renewal may result in prohibition of local business activity and administrative enforcement.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandatorily required for an International Company under the Vanuatu International Companies Act unless the company is licensed as a bank, insurance company, trustee, or otherwise subject to a specific VFSC supervisory requirement. The target entity, engaging in remote desk software and IoT telemetry, is not within a licensed activity and therefore no audit is compelled.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Companies Act permits preparation of financial statements under International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or other internationally recognized accounting principles as board-approved, including simplified local GAAP acceptable to the Registered Agent; records must be kept sufficient to reflect transactions and financial position.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the International Companies Act and VFSC rules, each International Company must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register at the registered office and file relevant beneficial ownership details with the VFSC. The Registered Agent must confirm beneficial ownership declarations on an annual basis or upon any share transfer affecting beneficial ownership. Any transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members and reflected in the next annual confirmation. Failure to keep the register updated may expose directors and the agent to penalties.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 – USD 1,200 per annum depending on agent and complexity
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No statutory audit required; if voluntarily audited, typical fee range for a small software entity is USD 1,500 – USD 4,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Vanuatu does not impose any corporate income tax or capital gains tax at national or provincial level. A Vanuatu International Company (VU IC) is expressly exempt from income tax, dividend withholding tax, business licence tax, and stamp duty on its worldwide activities. Tax exemption is automatic upon valid incorporation; no application, ruling, or concession is required. The only recurring government costs are the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission annual registration/renewal fee and licensed registered agent fees.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Not applicable — Vanuatu Revenue and Customs does not issue a corporate income tax return form. A VU IC has no CIT filing portal; only the VFSC 'International Company renewal' is required through the licensed registered agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No tax filing deadline applies. The VFSC annual renewal fee must be paid before strike-off commences; the exact due date is tied to the incorporation anniversary and VFSC administrative practice, monitored through the registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: No income tax return line items. The annual renewal statement confirms company name, registry number, registered office, registered agent, location of the register of directors/beneficial owners, and compliance with International Companies Act operating restrictions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders file nothing in Vanuatu; the registered agent files the annual renewal. No Vanuatu tax return, tax residence certificate, or CIT receipt is issued.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: VAT Return only if locally registrable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Where the IC makes taxable supplies to persons in Vanuatu and the value of supplies triggers VAT registration, a VAT return may be required. Cross-border remote screen-share and IOT telemetry services supplied to non-residents and settled through Stripe/Paddle are export services and normally outside Vanuatu VAT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A VU IC with no Vanuatu domestic turnover has no VAT registration obligation. Any local supply of software or support services must be reviewed against the Value Added Tax Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: No CIT late-filing penalties exist. Failure to pay the VFSC annual renewal within the prescribed period triggers a late penalty, suspension of good standing, and eventual striking-off from the register. A struck-off company cannot use payment rails, maintain bank accounts, or execute contracts; liabilities revive upon restoration.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — Vanuatu imposes no dividend withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Vanuatu has no comprehensive double-taxation agreement network. No Vanuatu tax-residence certificate or treaty-reduction form is required for dividends paid by a VU IC. For a dividend to a non-resident beneficiary, the recipient's residence country determines the tax treatment; the recipient may need to obtain its own foreign-tax-credit certificate or rely on its domestic participation exemption. Vanuatu will not withhold, transfer, or exit-tax the distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory withholding on both royalty and interest payments made by a Vanuatu IC. Because no DTA network exists, no reduced treaty rate applies. Royalties for software/IP and interest on related-party debt paid by a VU IC are free of Vanuatu withholding tax; they remain subject to taxation in the payee's jurisdiction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No Vanuatu statutory threshold in VUV. Vanuatu imposes no income tax and has no active transfer-pricing documentation obligation for a VU IC. However, to defend against CFC or economic-substance challenges, the IC should maintain transfer-pricing documentation in Local File/Master File style once related-party transactions exceed USD 1 million, using OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines as an administrative benchmark.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vanuatu implements international standards on harmful tax practices and can require substance for internationally mobile business models. A VU IC deriving revenue from remote screen-share software, IP licensing, or IOT telemetry should maintain real economic substance: a physical office, locally engaged management, board minutes in Vanuatu, operational staff performing core R&D/licensing functions, and adequate cash-flow and contract records. Absent such substance, foreign tax authorities may reallocate profits under CFC rules, while the IC risks being characterized as an abusive shell in the shareholder's home jurisdiction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating local Vanuatu VAT on domestic remote-support sales, using Stripe/Paddle to conceal related-party distributions, or falsely claiming that services are exported when materials, hardware, and end users are in Vanuatu.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of the full VAT shortfall plus statutory penalties (commonly up to 100% of the tax), civil fines, and criminal prosecution. Offences can lead to imprisonment and seizure of payment intermediary balances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally assessed for fraudulent participation, required to make restitution, subjected to asset-freezing orders, and, upon conviction, sentenced to imprisonment. A travel ban may be imposed pending extradition or criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing non-genuine remote-access or IOT subscriptions through Stripe/Paddle for third-party payers, layering funds among related entities, or failing to conduct know-your-customer review when acting as an informal money or value transfer service.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monetary penalties under Vanuatu's Financial Transactions Reporting Act and anti-money-laundering rules; freezing of accounts by the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit; revocation of any VFSC registration; criminal fines and imprisonment on conviction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners face criminal liability for money laundering if they knew or suspected the unlawful origin of funds; they can be held jointly liable for disgorgement, prohibited from managing companies, and subjected to travel bans and extradition requests.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive Shell Company / Lack of Commercial Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Holding all remote-screen-share and IOT telemetry software IP in a VU IC with no employees, no physical presence, no business decision-making, and no actual operation, while routing sales through Stripe/Paddle and extracting profits as inflated royalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Foreign tax authorities may deny tax residency, disregard the Vanuatu entity, reassess the enterprise in the parent jurisdiction, apply conduit-avoidance rules, and impose penalties of up to 200% of the tax understatement. Vanuatu authorities may strike off the IC for non-maintenance of the registered office and agent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts can pierce the corporate veil where the shell is a sham or fraud. Directors may be held liable for civil conspiracy, unjust enrichment, and restitution; in egregious cases they face winding-up examinations, disqualification, travel restrictions, and custodial sentences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the IC and third-party payment rails to invoice for 'remote IT support' supplied to sanctioned end-users, or generating false documentation to justify cross-border payments unrelated to genuine software services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violations expose Stripe/Paddle accounts to termination, fund holds, and blacklisting; enforcement authorities may impose severe civil penalties, seize proceeds, and refer individuals for criminal prosecution. The VFSC cooperates through international information exchange and regulatory assistance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who orchestrate false invoicing face criminal fraud sanctions, personal financial penalties equal to the value laundered, property restraint orders, and travel bans. In serious cases, extradition to the affected sanctioning jurisdiction is possible.
